cards.title: console.log() prints
cards.body: `console.log()` shows a value in the console, the text window where programs print. Text goes in quotes.

cards.title: One line each
cards.body: Each `console.log()` prints on its own line. The semicolon at the end marks the end of a statement.

cards.title: Every character counts
cards.body: The grader compares your output letter by letter, so capitals, commas and spaces all matter. `Hello` and `hello` are different.

cards.title: Spot the bug
cards.body: One of these lines crashes with a `TypeError`. Tap it.

bug.fix: JavaScript cares about capitals: it is `console.log`, not `console.Log`.

check.question: What does this print?
check.explanation: `+` joins the two strings exactly as they are, then `console.log()` prints the result without quotes.

exercise.prompt: Every programmer starts here. Print exactly `Hello, JavaScript!`
